context_requirements: Functional progesterone receptor (PGR) expression or other progestogen-responsive nuclear receptors such as NR3C2
Estrogen receptor (ESR1) expression for robust PGR induction and progesterone-responsive gene transcription
Intact glucocorticoid receptor (NR3C1) signaling for cross-talk with progestogens
Cell lines of breast or endometrial origin are more likely to respond
falsifiers: No significant transcriptional changes at 6 h or 24 h in any of the nine cell lines
Lack of induction of canonical progesterone-responsive genes such as FKBP5, TSC22D3, SGK1, or PGR in MCF7 cells
Predominant upregulation of pro-inflammatory genes (e.g., IL1B, CXCL2, CCL2) rather than the expected anti-inflammatory downregulation
Strong and uniform transcriptional response across all nine cell lines, including those lacking PGR expression

changes: Removed CCND1 and MYC from proximal_up and late_up because progestogens typically inhibit proliferation in responsive breast cancer cells, making their upregulation mechanistically inconsistent.
Removed CCND1 and MYC from late_up for the same reason.
Kept TSC22D3, ZFP36, EGR1, FOS, JUN, NFKBIA, TGFB3, SERPINE1, and MMP2 in proximal_up as they are supported by progestogen/glucocorticoid receptor signaling.
Kept anti-inflammatory and matrix genes in proximal_down and late_down as progestogens generally suppress these genes.
Retained generic_effects g1_arrest and proliferation_down as they are consistent with progestogen action.
Retained kinetics slow and magnitude weak at 6h, moderate at 24h as plausible for nuclear receptor-mediated transcription.
Retained line_response with MCF7 moderate and others weak, consistent with PGR/ESR1 expression patterns.
Retained context_requirements and falsifiers as they are appropriate for progestogen response.
Evidence list remains empty because no citations were provided.
